title: Nesting the CALCULATE that selects the lower-precedence item outside does not change the order: still 70
query: EVALUATE ROW ( "r", CALCULATE ( CALCULATE ( [Just2], Multiplier[Factor] = "Mul10" ), Adder[Addend] = "Plus5" ) )

source.quote: Nesting CALCULATE functions is not a way to change the order of application of calculation items, at least not in this example.
source.supports: the third puzzle: the outer Adder item has no effect on the inner CALCULATE and the code is identical to the second puzzle (70)

derivation: The only measure reference, [Just2], is evaluated inside the inner CALCULATE, where both items are selected: Multiplier (200) is applied first, then Adder: ( 2 + 5 ) * 10 = 70. The page's figure with the result is not in its text, hence derived.
